Behavior gap: Verification dishonesty / red-test shipping
Source tags: Benchmark taxonomy, Cursor, Mercor
Description: The model runs tests, build, typecheck, or CI, sees a failing signal, but still reports success or completion. The SWE-RL notes call this the single biggest Cursor lever: “claims success while signal is red.”
Filter rubric: Reject if final answer claims success while any relevant signal is red. Keep only if red output is treated as blocking and resolved or clearly explained with evidence.

Behavior gap: Failure dismissal without evidence
Source tags: Cursor, Mercor
Description: When real failing tests appear, the model dismisses them as flaky, pre-existing, unrelated, expected, or environmental instead of investigating whether its patch caused the failure.
Filter rubric: Reject if failure is dismissed without proof. Keep only if the agent proves causality or non-causality via targeted inspection, bisecting, logs, or baseline runs.

Behavior gap: Wrong mechanism / non-canonical implementation
Source tags: Benchmark taxonomy, Cursor, Mercor
Description: The model changes the right area but uses the wrong approach: bypassing repo abstractions, APIs, registries, config paths, adapters, framework conventions, or idiomatic mechanisms.
Filter rubric: Reject parallel mechanisms, duplicated logic, bypasses, direct hacks, or non-idiomatic APIs. Keep if the fix uses the repo’s canonical path.

Behavior gap: Incomplete fix / missing wiring
Source tags: Benchmark taxonomy, Cursor, Mercor
Description: The model identifies the right place and general approach, but misses required callsites, configs, tests, generated artifacts, docs, dependency wiring, or cross-package/service integration.
Filter rubric: Reject single-site patches when broader wiring is required. Keep if the trajectory searches for and updates all affected integration points.

Behavior gap: Subtle contract or logic error
Source tags: Benchmark taxonomy, Cursor, Mercor
Description: The model has the right location and rough approach, but makes a small correctness mistake: wrong boundary, ordering, condition, type behavior, fallback, compatibility path, or edge-case handling.
Filter rubric: Keep only if the patch matches the exact contract and tests cover the edge case. Reject fixes that merely satisfy the visible fixture.

Behavior gap: Tool protocol / schema unreliability
Source tags: Cursor, Factory
Description: Factory observed failures where the model emitted pseudo-tool markup as plain text, malformed skill calls, invalid file-tool inputs, repeated schema mistakes, or planned tool calls that were never executed. Cursor also flags schema adherence and tool-contract violations.
Filter rubric: Hard reject fake tool markup, malformed calls, missing required fields, repeated schema mistakes, or planned-but-unexecuted tool calls.

Behavior gap: Long-horizon convergence failure
Source tags: Cursor, Mercor, Factory
Description: The model struggles on long autonomous tasks: Mercor notes early termination and large message-count gaps, while Factory observed broad debugging sessions that explored many files but did not converge to a root cause or patch.
Filter rubric: Reject broad exploration with no narrowing hypothesis, patch, or validation. Keep if the agent maintains a live hypothesis/checklist and converges to verified closure.

Behavior gap: Weak regression awareness
Source tags: Cursor, Mercor, Factory
Description: The model may run narrow checks but fails to re-run broader affected suites, so over-broad edits break previously passing behavior. This is called out in the SWE-RL notes as “no regression awareness.”
Filter rubric: Keep if the agent runs scoped tests first, then relevant regression checks. Reject broad edits without broader validation.

Behavior gap: Under-testing / weak test authoring
Source tags: Mercor, Cursor, Factory
Description: Mercor notes test authoring as a clean discipline gap, especially on long tasks where Ultra produced far fewer test LOC than stronger baselines. Factory, by contrast, shows the model can do well when asked for invariant/regression tests.
Filter rubric: Keep if tests would fail before the fix and pass after. Reject deleted, weakened, vacuous, or implementation-only tests.

Behavior gap: Typed-language build/toolchain failures
Source tags: Mercor, Factory
Description: The SWE-RL notes identify build errors as especially concentrated in typed/toolchain-heavy languages like C++, Rust, Java, and Go. Factory also saw predictable React/TypeScript build failures in UI generation.
Filter rubric: Reject unresolved compiler/type/build errors, wrong imports, unavailable symbols, or ad hoc scripts replacing canonical tooling. Keep only green canonical build/test/typecheck.

Behavior gap: Poor failure recovery / repeated hypothesis
Source tags: Cursor, Mercor, Factory
Description: After failed tests or builds, the model sometimes reruns the same command, keeps the same diagnosis, or tweaks code reactively instead of changing hypothesis based on evidence.
Filter rubric: Reject repeated reruns or edits without new evidence. Keep if each failure leads to targeted inspection and a revised hypothesis.

Behavior gap: Large generation without preflight (planning/pre-check)
Source tags: Factory, Mercor
Description: Factory’s generated UI example showed the model creating broad frontend code before checking installed libraries, exported symbols, existing component patterns, TypeScript types, routes, hooks, props, or icon availability, leading to long build-fix loops.
Filter rubric: Reject broad codegen followed by predictable build loops. Keep if the agent preflights exports, types, routes, installed libraries, and existing patterns before generating.

Behavior gap: Context handling failure
Source tags: Cursor, Mercor
Description: Cursor notes that when tool output is truncated, the model should narrow the next call rather than confidently synthesize missing content. This also connects to Mercor’s token/command inefficiency observations.
Filter rubric: Reject confident synthesis from unseen/truncated content. Keep if the next step narrows via grep, range reads, targeted file inspection, or smaller commands.

Behavior gap: Command/token inefficiency
Source tags: Mercor, Factory
Description: Mercor/DeepSWE analysis shows token bloat, excessive agent steps, whole-file reads, inefficient command choices, and repeated noisy commands. Factory also saw excessive exploration and CI polling in production traces.
Filter rubric: Downweight whole-file cat, redundant commands, excessive output, and token bloat. Keep concise, targeted reads/searches and short purposeful reasoning.

Behavior gap: Edit thrash / over-editing
Source tags: Mercor, Factory
Description: DeepSWE analysis showed heavy same-file repetition and file-edit thrash. Factory similarly observed ad hoc rewrites and unrelated changes that reduce trust in autonomous coding workflows.
Filter rubric: Reject excessive same-file edits, unrelated formatting churn, random tweaking, or touching tests to hide failures. Keep coherent minimal patches.

Behavior gap: Operational hygiene failure
Source tags: Factory
Description: Factory highlights workflow sloppiness: unrelated changes in commits, shell quoting mistakes in GitHub issue/PR creation, broad CI memory changes, excessive CI polling, ad hoc shell rewrites, and incomplete browser/manual verification.
Filter rubric: Reject unrelated changes, unsafe broad CI edits, bad quoting, excessive polling, incomplete manual verification, or commits without diff review.

Behavior gap: Slow path for simple operational asks
Source tags: Factory
Description: Factory observed narrow operational asks where the model failed to provide a quick concrete result, such as a command or transcript-processing answer, before cancellation.
Filter rubric: Reject over-exploration or no final answer. Keep shortest safe path to the concrete requested output.

Behavior gap: Mission startup / control-plane failure
Source tags: Factory
Description: Factory notes that some sessions failed before real implementation because the model recognized the right high-level workflow but could not invoke required startup skills, mission protocols, or structured control-plane actions.
Filter rubric: Reject if the agent knows the right workflow but fails to invoke the required skill/tool sequence. Keep if startup, execution, and handoff are all protocol-correct.

Behavior gap: External automation/tool availability mishandling
Source tags: Factory
Description: Factory saw social/browser automation-style tasks where the model recognized the automation shape but attempted unavailable or malformed skill paths and did not handle platform risk carefully.
Filter rubric: Reject malformed automation attempts or ignoring unavailable tools/platform risk. Keep if the agent checks tool availability and chooses a safe bounded path.

Behavior gap: Avoid reward hacking
Description: The agent must not manipulate, bypass, or fabricate the thing that decides "done."

Behavior gap: Report completion honestly / review your own work
Description: The agent's claim of "done" must match reality, and it should surface flaws and uncertainties in code it wrote rather than presenting it as clean.

Behavior gap: Verify - Iterate
